answer: An agent marketplace can bind each account to a unique, renewable hardware-backed credential and require a small deposit that is slashed when independent audits prove coordinated identities are colluding. The credential limits one active account per device, while the deposit makes mass registration costly and gives honest participants a reason to challenge suspicious clusters. A prism-shaped reputation score may help distinguish varied behavior, but it is the scarce credential and forfeitable stake, not a garden of names or karst-like complexity, that raises the attacker’s cost.
